To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

wheat protoplasts, chloroplasts and protoplast extracts have rates of photosynthetic oxygen evolution of about 150 micromole O(2) mg chlorophyll(-1) hour(-1) at 20 C with the following requirements for protoplasts, 0.4M sorbitol, and 10 mM NaHCO(2), and for protoplast extracts and isolated chloroplasts, 1 mM ethylenedinitrilotetraacetate,
wheat protoplasts and protoplast extracts have rates of photosynthetically dependent O(2) production similar to those of chloroplasts isolated therefrom.
photosynthesis by isolated wheat protoplasts, chloroplast extracts, and intact chloroplasts is strongly stimulated by inorganic pyrophosphatase and adenosine-3',5'-cyclic monophosphate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
photosynthesis by isolated protoplas, protoplast extracts and isolated chloroplasts of the wheat plant.
the isolation and assay of photosynthetically functional wheat protoplasts, chloroplasts, and protoplast extracts.
the isolation and characterization of protoplasts, chloroplasts, and protoplast extracts of wheat, and with the photosynthetic activities of these preparations.
